text:
Connor Hellebuyck has had a heavier first season in New Jersey than anyone planned. He asked his way out of Winnipeg, then this month described threats against his family that, in Yahoo Sports' headline, "went beyond online death threats." On Saturday the Blues chased him after one period of a 9-6 loss. Mike Fink of The Hockey News reports he starts again tonight, his fifth in a row, at .897 and 0.7 goals below expected through nine games.

What makes the Devils maddening is how good the game in front of him has been. They take 57% of the expected goals at five on five (expected goals measure the quality of chances), they won the chance battle even in that 9-6 mess, and they sit 9.6 goals worse than expected in net as a team. Sheldon Keefe shuffled all four forward lines at practice, per Fink, with Lombardi moving to center. Anthony Mantha (throat fracture surgery) and Johnathan Kovacevic are out for at least a month. Timo Meier has goals in three straight, and Evan Rodrigues, eight points in his last ten, is one of our Sleepers.

Columbus comes in lighter after coming back from two down to win in Toronto on Saturday, with Matthew Knies back in the building he was traded out of. Cam Talbot gets a fourth straight start; he is 5.6 goals saved above expected, a long way from last season's -13.7. Zach Werenski has 11 points in ten and goals in three straight, and Kent Johnson a five-game point streak, but the Blue Jackets are seventh in the Metropolitan with a 9% playoff chance, and Werenski's name keeps surfacing in trade talk even as Yahoo reports he remains committed. Sean Monahan is still out. Mathieu Olivier, scoreless in eight on 2.8 expected goals, is one from 50 for his career.

Our numbers make New Jersey the stronger side tonight, 3.75 expected goals to 2.78. The question in Newark is simpler: whether the goalie they traded for can give them an ordinary night.
headline: Hellebuyck gets the net back after St. Louis
